Why_It_Matters_Here: Sets the global risk-free anchor. Every senior tranche we ever price is quoted as a spread over something that moves with this. Rising rates raise the return a private investor demands and make the concessional layer work harder for the same mobilisation.
Relevant if senior notes are placed with EU investors - which also triggers the risk-retention and qualified-investor rules in LIT-010.
Local funding cost for the Israel pilot site and the discount rate on any shekel-denominated structure.

The cleanest available proxy for whether investors are currently paid to take emerging-market credit risk. When spreads blow out, an unproven asset class does not get placed at any price - it is a go/no-go signal for issuance timing, not a pricing input.
Source: FRED (ICE BofA EM HY index OAS)

Why_It_Matters_Here: Whether the ABS market is open at all, and at what size. Directly informs the OQ-2 timing question - a technically viable pool still needs a functioning market to be placed into.

The single most direct macro link to PL-1 repayment. Food price spikes hit exactly the households in our target cohort, and they hit a whole region at once - which is correlated default risk, the parameter RT-5 is most sensitive to.

Leading indicator for drought and flood in East and Southern Africa, months ahead of the harvest failure it causes. If parametric insurance triggers are ever built (PL-1), this is the class of signal they key off.
Sub-national famine and food-insecurity outlooks. More actionable than a global price index because it is geographic - it tells you which cohort is about to come under stress.

PL-2 revenue is PPA-contracted, so spot prices do not hit revenue directly - but they move the tariff environment, the political appetite for renewables procurement, and the utility's own credit standing, which is the concentrated counterparty risk in that line.
Source: US EIA (and IEA for global outlooks)

Why_It_Matters_Here: A major income source for exactly the migrant-worker communities in the Israel pilot. A remittance disruption is a group-level shock and a candidate parametric trigger - one that is not weather-driven, which matters because weather triggers carry basis risk (LIT-007).

Determines whether concessional first-loss capital exists to be asked for. The whole structure in Memo 3 assumes a junior tranche someone is willing to fund; aid budget contraction is an existential input, not a background variable.

Indicator: Inflation and FX in target markets
Why_It_Matters_Here: Local-currency receivables against any hard-currency tranche is an unhedged mismatch. This is listed as a live risk in the business plan and is the input to whether local-currency tranches or DFI FX guarantees are needed.

The dominant pair for the Israel pilot. Any hard-currency tranche over shekel-denominated receivables is an unhedged mismatch, and this is the rate that mismatch is measured in. MAC-12 covers the euro leg, which only matters if notes are placed with EU investors.

The staple-grain sub-index of MAC-06. Worth tracking separately because it moves earlier and harder than the headline, and because staples are what the PL-1 cohort actually spends its marginal shekel or shilling on - a headline index diluted by meat and dairy understates the shock to a subsistence household.

The long-rate anchor. MAC-01 prices the short end, but a PL-2 PPA asset runs 15-25 years and is discounted off something much closer to the 10-year. The gap between the two is also the clearest single read on whether the curve is telling us long money is getting cheaper or dearer.

Sits behind two separate channels: the tariff and procurement environment for PL-2, and the fuel and fertiliser costs that feed into the food prices in MAC-06. One of the few places where the two product lines share a risk driver - which is worth knowing precisely because the diversification case for running both assumes they mostly do not.
